## Natural history notes

A native perennial herb in the mint family, characterized by square stems, opposite hairy leaves, and clusters of small pink, lavender, or whitish tubular flowers. Florida Hedgenettle grows in moist to moderately dry sandy soils, especially in flatwoods, disturbed uplands, roadsides, lawns, and other open habitats. It spreads aggressively through distinctive segmented underground tubers, which make the plant persistent and difficult to remove once established. The flowers attract bees, butterflies, and other pollinators, and flowering can occur from spring through fall. Although native to the southeastern United States, it is considered critically imperiled in South Florida.
